items.title: Wastewater surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in human populations: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of the concordance between wastewater and human resistance prevalence — protocol v1.0 and search strategies as executed (PROSPERO CRD420261520110)
items.abstract: Full protocol (PRISMA-P 2015) and search strategies as executed (PRISMA-S) for an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of the concordance between antimicrobial resistance (AMR) prevalence measured in wastewater and in human populations, extending Chau et al. 2022 (Environ Int 162:107171; PROSPERO CRD42019134946) to studies published from 1 January 2021, with extensions to genomic detection methods and low- and middle-income settings. Primary outcome: Lin's concordance correlation coefficient per organism-antimicrobial/gene comparison. Registered on PROSPERO as CRD420261520110 (published 11 October 2026). Deposited before title/abstract screening began. Contents: protocol v1.0 with a dated amendment log of all pre-screening changes; every database search string as executed on 16-18 October 2026 (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection and Preprint Citation Index, CAB Abstracts, Global Health) with dates, limits, hit counts and export checksums; forward citation tracking of the 34 seed studies; grey-literature sources; the title/abstract screening rubric and SOP; deterministic deduplication code and logs; and the known-item test against the 33 studies included by Chau et al. Searches identified 20,403 database records (7,059 unique) plus 1,506 new records from citation tracking: 8,565 records to title/abstract screening. Raw licensed database exports are not redistributed; their checksums are given. Screening decisions, the extraction dataset and analysis code will be deposited as a separate record at manuscript submission. AI use: a large-language-model assistant (Claude, Anthropic) was used under the guarantor's direction for drafting, operating database interfaces with the account holder signed in, deduplication code, and a non-deciding third title/abstract rating; all eligibility decisions are made by two human reviewers. Where this deposit and the PROSPERO record differ, the PROSPERO record is binding; differences are listed in the protocol's Appendix A. Version 1.1 will add the PRESS-reviewed search strategy; version 2.0 (at submission) adds the screening log, extraction dataset, risk-of-bias table and analysis code.

items.title: What Happens When Generative AI Enters College Data Analysis Education? Evaluating Changes in Students' Academic Self-Efficacy, Self-Regulated Learning, and Engagement
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to support learning in higher education, but evidence regarding changes in students' academic self-efficacy, self-regulated learning, and academic engagement remains limited. This study examined changes associated with a six-week generative AI-based data analysis education program among students at a three-year college in Wuhan, Hubei Province, China. A one-group pretest-posttest design was employed. Of 210 questionnaires distributed, 202 valid paired responses were analyzed. Academic self-efficacy, self-regulated learning, and academic engagement were measured using five-point Likert scales, with adapted items informed by established instruments. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson correlations, and paired-samples t tests were conducted. All three outcomes increased significantly: academic self-efficacy from 3.21 to 3.48 (dz = 0.38), self-regulated learning from 3.18 to 3.52 (dz = 0.51), and academic engagement from 3.35 to 3.66 (dz = 0.44). Posttest correlations among the outcomes were positive (r = 0.56-0.65, all p < .001). These findings suggest that structured AI-supported data analysis instruction may accompany improvements in students' confidence, learning regulation, and engagement. However, the one-group design cannot isolate the causal contribution of generative AI from other elements of the instructional program. Penelitian ini mengkaji perubahan yang berkaitan dengan program pembelajaran analisis data berbantuan AI generatif selama enam minggu pada mahasiswa perguruan tinggi vokasional tiga tahun di Wuhan, Provinsi Hubei, Tiongkok. Penelitian menggunakan desain satu kelompok dengan prates dan pascates. Dari 210 kuesioner yang dibagikan, sebanyak 202 respons berpasangan yang valid dianalisis. Ketiga konstruk diukur menggunakan skala Likert lima poin dengan butir adaptasi yang mengacu pada instrumen yang telah dikembangkan sebelumnya. Analisis meliputi statistik deskriptif, reliabilitas, korelasi Pearson, dan uji t berpasangan. Seluruh konstruk mengalami peningkatan yang signifikan: efikasi diri akademik dari 3,21 menjadi 3,48 (dz = 0,38), regulasi diri dalam belajar dari 3,18 menjadi 3,52 (dz = 0,51), serta keterlibatan akademik dari 3,35 menjadi 3,66 (dz = 0,44). Korelasi antarkonstruk pada pascates bersifat positif (r = 0,56-0,65; seluruh p < 0,001). items.title: What is the role of the SEIPS framework when assessing digital health technology? A scoping review
items.abstract: Digital health tools are systems, technologies, and services based on information and communications technology designed to improve healthcare delivery, patient engagement, and the management of health information. Digital tools encompass a broad range of applications that facilitate remote care, data sharing, diagnostics, and health monitoring (Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, 2024). For example, electronic health records, health tracking apps, telemedicine (Livieri et al., 2025), and clinical decision support (Newton et al., 2025). The benefits include improved access and convenience for patients, enhanced efficiency, improved accuracy and decision making, and cost savings. However, challenges such as usability issues and disparities in access exist (Livieri et al., 2025), which can impact patient safety. Human Factors (HF) approaches can be used to examine and improve patient safety within complex systems such as digital health (Carayon 2022). For example, the Systems Engineering Initiative for Patient Safety (SEIPS) framework has been widely used to guide research, evaluate and improve healthcare systems and patient safety. The model provides a comprehensive, Human Factors-based approach that considers the complex interactions among people, technology, tasks, environment, and organisational factors (Carayon et al., 2006). SEIPS provides a holistic visual representation of work as done to build organisation awareness, describe systems, and allows the identification of barriers and facilitators (of what) within work processes, thereby supporting redesign and improvements. Despite the growing emphasis on HF and systems thinking in healthcare, its integration into the design and implementation if digital health interventions such as clinical decision support systems remains inconsistent (O’Dea et al., 2025). Digital tools that are developed and implemented without consideration of existing work systems such as workflows, roles, and the environment often fail to integrate smoothly which can lead to inefficiencies, user frustration, and low adoption rates (Marwaha et al., 2022). The holistic, systems-based approach of the SEIPS framework makes it well-suited to guide and evaluate digital health interventions. Although SEIPS has been applied across a range of health care settings, its use in digital health research appears heterogenous and underexamined. A comprehensive review of the literature is therefore needed to map the extent and nature of SEIPS applications in this context, identify gaps in knowledge, and inform future research and practice.

items.title: What makes human service distinctly human in the AI era? Conceptualizing and measuring authentic relational service competency
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) service agents increasingly simulate human interaction, the basis for distinguishing human service has become theoretically ambiguous. While prior research consistently identifies authenticity as a key limitation of AI-enabled service, authenticity remains underdeveloped as a uniquely human service capability. Addressing this gap, we introduce Authentic Relational Service (ARS) as a distinct form of service through which frontline employees create genuine, contextually responsive, and relationship-centered customer interactions. We further conceptualize authenticity as a competency-based capability and develop a measure of Authentic Relational Service Competency (ARSC), which enables frontline employees to enact ARS. Using established scale-development procedures, this study identifies and validates four dimensions of ARSC: perspective-taking, patience, creativity, and agility. By conceptualizing and operationalizing Authentic Relational Service as a distinct human service capability, this research advances theory on human-AI service differentiation and provides a foundation for understanding uniquely human value creation in service contexts.
